{{verse|chapter=3|verse=9}}† Vvhat then? do vve excel them? No, not so. For vve haue argued the Ievves and the Greekes, al to be vnder sinne: {{verse|chapter=3|verse=10}}† as it is vvritten: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 13, 1. 52, 3.''}}* ''That there is {{sup|‖}} not any man iust'', {{verse|chapter=3|verse=11}}† ''there is not that vnderstandeth, there is not that seeketh after God''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=12}}† ''Al haue declined, they are become vnprofitable together: there is not that doeth good, there is not so much as one''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 5, 11.''}}* ''Their throte is an open sepulchre, vvith their tonges they dealt deceitefully. '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 139, 4.''}}* ''The venim '' {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ c ''Aspidum,'' A kinde of litle serpents.}}∷ ''of aspes vnder their lippes''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=14}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 9, 7. Es. 19, 7.''}}* ''Vvhose mouth is ful of malediction and bitternes'': {{verse|chapter=3|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Pro. 1, 16.''}}* ''Their feete svvift to shede bloud''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=16}}† ''Destruction and infelicitie in their vvaies'': {{verse|chapter=3|verse=17}}† ''and the vvay of peace they haue not knovven''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=18}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 35, 2.''}}* ''There is no feare of God before their eies''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=19}}† And vve knovv that vvhatsoeuer the Lavv speaketh, to them it speaketh that are in the Lavv: that euery mouth may be stopped, and al the vvorld may be made subiect to God: {{verse|chapter=3|verse=20}}† because {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gal. 2, 16.''}}* {{sup|‖}} by the vvorkes of the Lavv no flesh shal be iustified before him. For by the Lavv is the knovvledge of sinne.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=21}}† But novv vvithout the Lavv the iustice of God is manifested: testified by the lavv and the Prophets. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=22}}† And the {{sup|‖}} iustice of God by faith of {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}, vnto al and vpō al that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ To beleeue in him, here compriseth not only the act of faith, but of hope & charitie, as the Apostle explicateth him self. ''Galat. 5, 6''.}}∷ beleeue in him. For there is no distinction. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=23}}† For al haue sinned: and doe neede the glorie of God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=24}}† Iustified {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ No man atteineth his first Iustification by the merites either of his faith or workes, but merely by Christes grace and mercie: though his faith & vvorkes proceding of grace be dispositions & preparations thereunto.}}∷ gratis by his grace, by the redemption that is in {{sc|Christ Iesvs}}, {{verse|chapter=3|verse=25}}† vvhom God hath proposed a {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`propitiatour''}}`propitiation', by faith in his bloud, to the shevving of his iustice, for the remission of former sinnes, {{verse|chapter=3|verse=26}}† in the toleration of God, to the shevving of his iustice in this time: that he may be iust, and iustifying him that is of the faith of {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=27}}† VVhere is then thy boasting? it is excluded. by vvhat lavv? of deedes? No, but by the lavv of faith. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=28}}† For vve account a man to be iustified{{sup|‖}} by faith vvithout the vvorkes of the Lavv. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=29}}† Is he God of the Ievves only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes of the Gentiles also. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=30}}† For it is one God, that iustifieth circumcision by faith, and prepuce by faith. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=31}}† Do vve then destroy the Lavv by faith? God forbid. but vve do establish the Lavv.
